item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Voyager One Against the References

turns.text: Make a silent 9-second widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1, using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Three equal-length scenes: 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Keep 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible. Show the probe near Earth, Jupiter, then Saturn; match its real dish-and-boom design. Don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

item.tests: Tests whether a factual film matches a named reference in dates, mission identity, spacecraft appearance and scene order.

answer_sheet.Facts to include: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977, flew by Jupiter in 1979 and flew by Saturn in 1980.
answer_sheet.Length and scene order: 9 seconds total: three 3-second scenes showing Earth, Jupiter and Saturn in that order.
answer_sheet.Wording: Use exactly the five supplied labels. Keep Voyager 1 and Source: NASA Science visible throughout.
answer_sheet.Sound: Completely silent, with no narration, music or sound effects.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Your call, provided the spacecraft matches the real dish-and-boom design and the planets are recognizable.

must_haves: Three scenes appear in order, each lasting approximately three seconds: probe near Earth, near Jupiter, then near Saturn.
Each scene displays its corresponding date caption exactly, with 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout.
The probe consistently has Voyager's large circular communications dish and projecting instrument booms, not solar-panel wings or a generic satellite body.
Jupiter is visibly banded and Saturn has prominent rings; neither is replaced with Uranus or Neptune.
The output contains no Uranus or Neptune flyby claims and no conflicting dates.

turns.text: Please make a widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1 using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . I've always found this mission fascinating, and I'm a little worried about getting the two Voyager spacecraft mixed up when explaining it. What I have in mind is 9 seconds total, completely silent with no narration, music, or sound effects, split into three equal 3-second scenes showing the probe near Earth, then Jupiter, then Saturn. The scene labels should be exactly 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', and 'Saturn flyby: 1980', in that order. Please also keep the exact labels 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout, so those and the three scene labels are the five supplied labels to use. The visual style is up to you as long as the planets are recognizable and the probe matches its real dish-and-boom design, and please don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

opening.text: Please make a widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1 using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . I've always found this mission fascinating, and I'm a little worried about getting the two Voyager spacecraft mixed up when explaining it. What I have in mind is 9 seconds total, completely silent with no narration, music, or sound effects, split into three equal 3-second scenes showing the probe near Earth, then Jupiter, then Saturn. The scene labels should be exactly 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', and 'Saturn flyby: 1980', in that order. Please also keep the exact labels 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout, so those and the three scene labels are the five supplied labels to use. The visual style is up to you as long as the planets are recognizable and the probe matches its real dish-and-boom design, and please don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.
